question: What is the smallest real-corpus evaluation that can tell us whether the current KAD research workflow produces useful, traceable, reproducible research artifacts without prematurely building a larger knowledge platform?

evaluated_options.name: Synthetic Mock Corpus Evaluation
cons: Fails to exercise authentic bibliographic and content variability

evaluated_options.name: Large-Scale Multi-Domain Academic Corpus (>50 papers)
cons: Prematurely builds knowledge platform scale before verifying core workflow primitives

evaluated_options.name: Bounded 5-Source Real Corpus on Deterministic Agent Control & Evidence-Grounded Execution
pros: Uses 100% real published academic literature with canonical DOIs and arXiv identifiers
Directly relevant to KAD-PI architecture (deterministic agents, verifiable tools, reflection loops, test-driven validation)
Sufficient to exercise all 10 target workflow capabilities end-to-end
Exercises verified sources, preprints, deduplication, citation linkage, and graceful degradation
Minimal bounded footprint adhering strictly to TOKENMAXXING
cons: Requires curated source texts and extraction manifests

rationale: Option C provides authentic empirical evidence of research workflow fidelity on real scientific papers while remaining strictly bounded and token-efficient. It exercises all 10 pipeline capabilities without premature infrastructure expansion.
